4099.title: Saving Painted Textures in Blender
4099.heading: Saving Painted Textures in Blender
4099.content:
A texture painted in Blender must be saved as an external image if it is to persist independently of the current in-memory image buffer. The Image Editor's Save As command chooses its location and format.

The UV layout can also be exported as an image, providing a guide for work in another painting application. A lossless format such as PNG preserves the painted result while keeping file size manageable.

Saving is a separate step from painting because edits can remain only in Blender's image buffer. The artist should verify the active canvas and destination after a session so the material continues to find the intended image in later Blender or game-engine work.

4102.title: Scalability
4102.heading: Scalability
4102.content:
Scalability is an application's ability to continue serving useful work as demand increases. It depends on how requests consume constrained resources such as server threads, database round trips, memory, and network transfer.

Paging, asynchronous I/O, caching, and fewer queries address different constraints. Load testing shows whether a chosen change improves the behavior that matters rather than merely relocating the bottleneck.

Scaling can be [[Horizontal Scalability|horizontal]], by changing the number of resource instances, or [[Vertical Scalability|vertical]], by increasing the capacity of an individual resource. Cloud [[Rapid Elasticity|elasticity]] automates horizontal scaling in and out so that capacity can follow demand.

4105.content:
The saturation (J:I∞) consists of elements r for which Iⁿr is contained in J for some nonnegative integer n. It is the union of the ideal quotients (J:Iⁿ).

Saturation removes components supported where I vanishes. The source computes it through polynomial elimination by adjoining variables that encode inverses, linking it to [[Ring Localization]] and [[Elimination Ideal]]s.

4108.sourceSearchName: satellite based augmentation system satellite based augmentation system
4108.title: Satellite-Based Augmentation System
4108.heading: Satellite-Based Augmentation System
4108.content: A satellite-based augmentation system uses surveyed reference stations to monitor GNSS errors across a region, processes those observations into corrections and integrity information, and rebroadcasts the result through geostationary satellites. The user receives both the original navigation signals and a regional assessment of their quality. This architecture extends differential positioning over a wide area and supports safety-critical operations without requiring a local correction transmitter at every site.

4111.title: Satellite Ephemeris
4111.heading: Satellite Ephemeris
4111.content: A satellite ephemeris is the set of orbital parameters from which a receiver computes the satellite's position and velocity at a particular time. GPS ground stations estimate these parameters from observations and predict the orbit forward before uploading the data for broadcast. The prediction must account for effects such as Earth's equatorial bulge, lunar gravity, and solar radiation pressure. A range measurement is useful only when the transmitting point in space is also known accurately.

4114.title: SAS Procedure
4114.heading: SAS Procedure
4114.content:
A SAS procedure, conventionally invoked with a `PROC` statement, is a packaged operation for analysis, reporting, plotting, or data management. Procedures such as PROC FREQ, PROC UNIVARIATE, and PROC LOGISTIC each expose their own options while sharing a broad call-and-argument structure.

Procedures contrast with the [[SAS Data Step]], which edits records, and often rely on the [[SAS Output Delivery System]] when results must become reusable datasets or presentation files. This division means that a complete SAS analysis may require familiarity with several related command systems.

4116.sourceSearchName: sas output delivery system sas output delivery system
4116.title: SAS Output Delivery System
4116.heading: Document

4117.sourceSearchName: sas output delivery system sas output delivery system
4117.title: SAS Output Delivery System
4117.heading: SAS Output Delivery System
4117.content:
The SAS Output Delivery System, or ODS, routes procedure output into destinations such as HTML, report files, or SAS datasets. It is often required when a table displayed by a [[SAS Procedure]] must be captured for later processing or exported to a spreadsheet.

ODS adds a distinct layer of syntax to an analysis. The captured dataset may contain every statistic generated by the procedure in a structure unlike the desired journal table, so further reshaping is usually necessary before presentation.

4118.title: SAS Output Delivery System

4120.heading: Sampling-Based Clustering
4120.content:
Sampling-based clustering derives a smaller representative subset, clusters it, and uses the result to characterize or assign the full dataset. The reduced problem can fit in one machine and finish much sooner.

The approximation is reliable only when the sample preserves rare groups, density differences, and boundary structure important to the analysis.

4123.title: SAS Macro
4123.heading: SAS Macro
4123.content:
A SAS macro is reusable code written in SAS macro language to generate or repeat procedural operations. Macros accept parameters, expand into SAS statements, and commonly automate recurring data-management, analysis, or reporting tasks.

Macro language is a separate layer beside procedures and data steps. An R workflow usually approaches the same need through [[Statistical Function Automation]], iteration, or apply-family functions rather than reproducing SAS macro syntax directly.

4125.title: SAS Data Step

4126.sourceSearchName: sas data step sas data step
4126.title: SAS Data Step
4126.heading: SAS Data Step
4126.content:
The SAS data step is a procedural language for creating or editing datasets one observation at a time. SAS implicitly loops through qualifying rows, applies the statements in the step, and writes the resulting observations to one or more output datasets.

Because execution is record-oriented, sorting and careful code design can strongly affect performance. The data step is powerful but differs conceptually from R's object operations and from declarative query systems, which specify a result while leaving execution planning to an optimizer.

4127.title: SAS Data Step

4129.title: Sampling Distribution
4129.heading: Sampling Distribution
4129.content:
A sampling distribution is the probability distribution of a statistic across repeated samples drawn by the same procedure. It describes how an estimator varies even though the population parameter remains fixed.

Statistical theory and simulation both approximate this distribution. Its center indicates systematic bias, while its spread is the statistic's [[Standard Error]] and provides the basis for tests and confidence intervals.

4132.title: Sample Size Calculation
4132.heading: Sample Size Calculation
4132.content:
A sample size calculation solves for the number of observations required after the analyst specifies the planned test, effect size, significance level, target power, and allocation structure. The result may refer to each group or to the total sample, depending on the function.

The computed number should be rounded up and adjusted for expected attrition, missing measurements, clustering, or unequal outcome groups. It is a design estimate based on assumptions, not a guarantee that the completed study will yield a significant result.

4135.title: Salient Image Feature
4135.heading: Salient Image Feature
4135.content:
A salient image feature is a local point or region whose intensity structure is distinctive enough to be found reliably after modest image transformation. Corners and textured junctions are more useful than flat areas because their neighborhoods can be localized in multiple directions.

Clone detectors use a sparse set of such features to avoid comparing every pixel block. Each feature receives a descriptor that supports fast matching, after which the spatial relationship between matched features supplies evidence for or against duplication.

4138.title: SAGE Air Defense System
4138.heading: SAGE Air Defense System
4138.content:
SAGE was a network of large computers built to combine radar data and calculate interception paths for incoming bombers. Its development funded advances in memory, displays, communications, and interactive computing.

The system was operational as ballistic missiles reduced the relevance of its original mission. Its technical legacy nevertheless influenced IBM computers and later human-computer interfaces.

4141.title: Saddle Point
4141.heading: Saddle Point
4141.content:
A saddle point is a [[Stationary Point]] that is neither a local maximum nor a local minimum. The function increases in some nearby directions and decreases in others.

For a twice-differentiable function, an indefinite [[Hessian Matrix]] identifies this mixed curvature. A zero gradient alone therefore does not establish an optimum.

4144.title: S-Polynomial
4144.heading: S-Polynomial
4144.content:
An S-polynomial combines two polynomials so that their leading terms cancel. Multipliers derived from the least common multiple of the leading monomials align those terms before subtraction.

S-polynomials expose conflicts between different possible reductions. [[Buchberger's Algorithm]] repeatedly reduces them; a generating set is a [[Gröbner Basis]] when all required S-polynomials reduce to zero.

4147.title: Rutherford Scattering
4147.heading: Rutherford Scattering
4147.content: Rutherford scattering directs alpha particles at a thin foil and measures their deflections. Most pass nearly straight through, while a small fraction scatter through large angles. The pattern shows that atoms are mostly empty space and that positive charge and most mass are concentrated in a compact nucleus rather than spread throughout the atom.

4153.title: Runtime Reconfiguration
4153.heading: Runtime Reconfiguration
4153.content:
Runtime reconfiguration changes an application's component connections, parameters, scripts, or device bindings while the AR system is running. Developers can inspect live values and adjust the pipeline without repeatedly rebuilding and restarting a complex physical setup.

This supports rapid prototyping and adaptation when sensors or environments change. Reconfiguration must preserve type, dependency, and consistency rules so an experimental change does not leave the real-time system in an invalid state.

4156.title: Rumor Veracity
4156.heading: Rumor Veracity
4156.content:
Rumor veracity is the truth status eventually assigned to an initially unverified claim. Possible outcomes include true, false, disputed, complex, or still unknown rather than only a simple binary label.

Propagation size and speed do not determine veracity because the same communication mechanisms carry accurate and inaccurate information. Evidence from content, sources, user reactions, and outside confirmation must be evaluated separately.

4159.title: Running Mean Overlay
4159.heading: Running Mean Overlay
4159.content: A running mean overlay adds a locally averaged line to a [[Time Plot]]. Each displayed average summarizes a moving neighborhood of observations, reducing short-term variation so slower movement becomes easier to see. Window width controls the tradeoff: a wider window produces a smoother line but can suppress or displace brief events. The raw series should remain visible because the overlay is a transformation, not an independent measurement.

4162.title: Rumor Source
4162.heading: Rumor Source
4162.content:
A rumor source is the node from which a particular diffusion process begins. It may be the creator of the claim or simply the earliest origin represented inside the observed network.

The source is usually hidden once only a later [[Infection Snapshot]] is available. Missing nodes, delayed observation, heterogeneous transmission, and multiple origins make reconstruction uncertain.

4165.sourceSearchName: rumor source detection rumor source detection
4165.title: Rumor Source Detection
4165.heading: Rumor Source Detection
4165.content:
Rumor source detection estimates the origin of a diffusion from the network, a spreading model, and observed affected nodes. Candidate sources are compared by how plausibly their paths and timing could have produced the snapshot.

Many estimators assume homogeneous infection and recovery, but real networks and observations are incomplete. The result is therefore conditional on both the diffusion model and the available observer set.

4168.title: Rumor Propagation
4168.heading: Rumor Propagation
4168.content:
Rumor propagation is the movement of an unverified claim as people publish, forward, criticize, verify, or retract it. Online participants act as both producers and consumers, permitting rapid transmission to targeted audiences.

The process varies with network structure, user actions, truth status, and uncertainty. A propagation model describes how nodes change state, while content analysis addresses what the message says.

4170.heading: Document
4170.content:

4171.title: Rumor Centrality
4171.heading: Rumor Centrality
4171.content:
Rumor centrality ranks candidate sources by the number or likelihood of diffusion orderings consistent with an observed infected subgraph. The most central candidate is treated as the source estimate under the assumed spreading model.

Its guarantees depend on conditions such as a tree-like network and homogeneous transmission. Recovery, cycles, partial observations, and multiple sources require extensions or different estimators.

4173.title: Rumor Cascade

4173.content:

4174.title: Rumor Cascade
4174.heading: Rumor Cascade
4174.content:
A rumor cascade is the branching sequence of users and transmissions through which an unverified claim spreads. Its depth, breadth, timing, and participating communities describe propagation separately from the claim's truth value.

Rumors and non-rumors can travel through the same network, so a large cascade is not proof of falsity. Comparisons must control for topic, audience, observation window, and platform behavior.

4177.title: Rumor Annotation
4177.heading: Rumor Annotation
4177.content:
Rumor annotation assigns structured labels to messages or events so propagation and veracity can be studied. Labels may distinguish rumor from non-rumor, record disputed or unknown truth values, and identify supporting, questioning, or correcting reactions.

Annotation converts qualitative judgments into training and evaluation data. Its reliability depends on clear definitions, evidence available to annotators, and agreement among independent judgments.

Rule-based access control grants or denies access according to conditions defined by policy. A rule may test time, location, system state, network origin, or another contextual property surrounding the attempted operation.

The decision is based on the rule's current truth rather than only the claimant's fixed role. It can be combined with [[Role-Based Authorization]] when both job responsibility and environmental conditions matter.

4183.heading: Rule of Recognition
4183.content:
A rule of recognition supplies criteria for identifying which norms count as valid law within a legal system. Officials use it to distinguish authoritative rules from other commands, customs, or moral claims.

It is a secondary rule because it governs the status of primary obligations rather than prescribing ordinary conduct directly. Its role helps explain how a legal order can be analyzed as a structured practice.

4186.title: Rule of Change
4186.heading: Rule of Change
4186.content:
A rule of change specifies who may introduce, alter, or repeal legal rules and which procedures make those changes valid. It allows a legal order to adapt deliberately rather than depending only on slow shifts in custom.

As a secondary rule, it constrains the creation of new powers and duties. In data-intensive environments, it also frames how legal protections can respond to new forms of observation and automated action.

4189.title: Rule Induction
4189.heading: Rule Induction
4189.content:
Rule induction extracts conditional if-then relationships from data, often using statistical significance, tree paths, or frequent co-occurrence. The result is an interpretable set of conditions associated with outcomes or classes.

Induced rules summarize observed regularities rather than guaranteed causal laws. Their support, accuracy, stability, and domain plausibility must be assessed before operational use.

4192.heading: Rule of Adjudication
4192.content:
A rule of adjudication identifies who may decide whether a legal rule has been violated and how that decision is made. It supplies procedures and authority for resolving disputes about primary obligations.

The rule is secondary because it organizes application and enforcement. Effective privacy protection requires more than a written duty; it also requires an institution able to determine violations and provide a remedy.

4195.title: Rubber-Sheet Stereo Conversion
4195.heading: Rubber-Sheet Stereo Conversion
4195.content: The rubber-sheet method maps an extracted image onto a subdivided flat plane and uses a grayscale depth map to displace that plane in 3D. Levels or grade reshape how far different features protrude. Two virtual cameras then record the slightly different left and right views needed for stereo presentation. Unlike a simple horizontal 2D displacement, the second view comes from viewing an actual deformed surface. The result still depends on accurate extraction and the authored depth map, as explained in [[Roto-Gradient Depth Maps for Stereo]].

4198.title: Rule Introduction
4198.heading: Rule Introduction
4198.content:
Rule introduction is the first designed encounter through which a player learns what a rule or object means. That encounter establishes expectations that will influence every later use of the element.

A clear introduction isolates the important behavior, gives the player a reason to interact, and makes consequences observable without imposing an excessive setback. New objects are safest to combine only after their individual behaviors and relationships to existing [[Game Verb|verbs]] are understood.

4201.title: RStudio
4201.heading: RStudio
4201.content:
RStudio is an integrated development environment for R that combines source editing, execution, debugging, project tools, and application-building support. It runs R rather than replacing the R language or its package ecosystem.

The extra interface is valuable for development tasks such as deploying interactive applications, but a basic R interface may be sufficient for a focused, hypothesis-driven analysis. The choice should follow the workflow's needs rather than be treated as a statistical difference.

In the book's working layout, [[RStudio]] brings the source editor, [[R Console]], environment, files, plots, packages, and [[R Help System]] into coordinated panes. That arrangement supports an iterative path from inspection to reusable script without making console history the authoritative analysis.

4204.title: RStudio Server
4204.heading: RStudio Server
4204.content:
RStudio Server provides the RStudio development environment through a web browser while R executes on a remote machine. It lets multiple analysts use centrally managed computation and packages without moving every dataset to a desktop.

Its browser interface preserves the familiar editor, console, environment, files, plots, packages, and help panes of [[RStudio]].

4210.title: Row Proportion
4210.heading: Row Proportion
4210.content:
A row proportion divides a cell in a [[Contingency Table]] by the total for its row. It answers questions framed within the row category, such as what proportion of veterans report asthma.

Row and column proportions are not interchangeable. The grouping variable that supplies the denominator should follow the scientific question, and the table's orientation must be documented so readers do not reverse the conditional comparison.

4213.sourceSearchName: row echelon form row echelon form
4213.title: Row Echelon Form
4213.heading: Row Echelon Form
4213.content:
A matrix is in row echelon form when zero rows are at the bottom, every nonzero row begins with a leading one, and each leading one lies to the right of the leading one above it.

As an [[Augmented Matrix]], this form exposes pivots and free variables. The corresponding [[Linear System]] can be solved from the last nonzero row upward by [[Back Substitution]].

4216.sourceSearchName: row and column masses row and column masses
4216.title: Row and Column Masses
4216.heading: Row and Column Masses
4216.content:
After dividing a table by its grand total, each row mass is its share of all recorded occurrences and each column mass is an attribute's corresponding share. These marginal distributions provide empirical weights for the two clouds of points used in correspondence analysis.

Mass is not simply a display size. It helps define the chi-squared profile distance and the moment of inertia around a cloud's center. A text segment and a word thus enter the factor mapping through both a conditional profile and a weight derived from their frequency in the whole table.

4219.title: Route Redirect
4219.heading: Route Redirect
4219.content:
A route redirect replaces one client location with another. It is useful for assigning a canonical starting route, preserving an old route, or moving the user after authentication or successful form submission.

The redirect changes navigation state rather than rendering the destination page inside the old route. React Router then matches the new location to its declared component.

4222.title: Route Parameter
4222.heading: Route Parameter
4222.content:
A route parameter is a variable segment embedded in a route path, such as the identifier in a question URL. When a location matches, React Router supplies the captured text to the rendered component.

The component converts and validates the value before using it to fetch a resource. An effect that depends on the parameter reruns when navigation changes that value without replacing the component type.

4225.title: Route Guard
4225.heading: Route Guard
4225.content:
An Angular route guard decides whether a client-side route may be activated, loaded, or left under the current application state. An authentication guard can redirect an unauthenticated user to a login flow before showing a protected component.

Route guards improve navigation behavior but run in the client and can be bypassed. The server endpoint reached by the guarded component must enforce its own [[Authorization]].

4228.title: Route Declaration
4228.heading: Route Declaration
4228.content:
A route declaration associates a URL path pattern with the React component that should render for it. A collection of declarations forms the navigable structure of the client application.

Ordering and exact matching matter because a broad path may otherwise match before a more specific one. Parameter segments allow one declaration to represent many resource-specific locations.

4231.title: Rounding
4231.heading: Rounding
4231.content:
Rounding replaces a number with the nearest representable value at the retained precision. The first discarded digit determines whether the final retained digit is increased.

Its error is generally no more than half a unit in the last retained place. Repeated operations can still accumulate or amplify these small [[Round-Off Error|round-off errors]].

4234.sourceSearchName: round off error round off error
4234.title: Round-Off Error
4234.heading: Round-Off Error
4234.content:
Round-off error is the difference introduced when an exact number or arithmetic result is replaced by a finite-precision representation.

Subtraction of nearly equal numbers can expose it through cancellation, and multiplication or division can propagate it. A large [[Matrix Condition Number]] can amplify small data or rounding errors into a large solution error.

Rough missing-value imputation fills gaps with a simple representative value, such as a numeric median or a common category, to let an exploratory model run. It is a pragmatic diagnostic step rather than a substitute for a principled missing-data analysis.

The resulting model should be labeled accordingly because simple fills can shrink variation and distort relationships.

In motion, the shapes must follow each scene element rather than describe only one still frame. Avoid pure black and white so later grade adjustments have room to change the depth. 4243.title: Rotini Fin Geometry
4243.heading: Rotini Fin Geometry
4243.content:
Rotini fin geometry twists an extended surface along its length, creating a helical or pasta-like form with greater surface complexity than a straight cylindrical or rectangular fin. A parameterized sweep or comparable construction controls pitch, cross section, length, and total twist.

The twist changes surface area and heat-flow paths while making meshing more demanding. Equal-volume comparison with a simpler fin separates geometric distribution from the trivial effect of adding more material.

4246.title: Rootkit
4246.heading: Rootkit
4246.content:
A rootkit is a collection of techniques or software that preserves privileged, concealed access to a compromised system. It can alter or evade ordinary system reporting so that malicious processes, files, or connections are harder to observe.

Rootkits attack confidence in the host's own evidence, making [[System Integrity Verification]] especially important. Recovery may require inspection from a trusted environment or complete restoration rather than relying only on the affected operating system.

4248.sourceSearchName: root of an equation root of an equation
4248.title: Root of an Equation
4248.heading: Document

4249.sourceSearchName: root of an equation root of an equation
4249.title: Root of an Equation
4249.heading: Root of an Equation
4249.content:
A root of an equation $f(x)=0$ is a value of $x$ at which the function vanishes. Root-finding converts many nonlinear equations into the task of locating such a zero.

[[Bisection Method]] brackets a root using a sign change, while [[Newton Root-Finding Method]] uses local derivative information. A root is not automatically an optimum unless it is a zero of an appropriate derivative and passes further tests.

4250.sourceSearchName: root of an equation root of an equation
4250.title: Root of an Equation
4250.heading: References

4252.title: Root
4252.heading: Root
4252.content:
An (m)th root reverses an (m)th power. If (a=b^m), then (b) is an (m)th root of (a), written

$$b=\sqrt[m]{a}.$$

The number (m\geq2) is the root's index and (a) is the quantity under the root symbol. An index of two is normally omitted, producing a [[Square Root]], while an index of three gives a [[Cube Root]]. Root extraction can produce an [[Irrational Number]] even when the original value is a natural number.

4255.sourceSearchName: role based authorization role based authorization
4255.title: Role-Based Authorization
4255.heading: Role-Based Authorization
4255.content:
Role-based authorization grants or denies an operation according to a role associated with the authenticated user. It allows two users who can both enter an application to receive different capabilities.

The stock checker separates read and update permissions so staff roles can expose only the operations each job requires. Server enforcement protects the API, while matching UI changes avoid presenting controls that the current user cannot successfully invoke.

In an operating-system security model, role-based control groups permissions by user category, such as a general user or administrator. Changing the role changes the available operations without requiring an independent rule for every user-resource pair.
links: Operating System Security and Access Control

4257.heading: Document

4258.sourceSearchName: root of a polynomial root of a polynomial
4258.title: Root of a Polynomial
4258.heading: Root of a Polynomial
4258.content:
A root of a polynomial a(x) over a field extension is an element c for which a(c) = 0. A degree-n polynomial over a field has at most n distinct roots.

Roots connect evaluation homomorphisms, linear factors, field extensions, and factorization.

4261.title: Root Field
4261.heading: Root Field
4261.content:
A root field of a polynomial over K is a smallest extension containing all of the polynomial's roots. The polynomial splits into linear factors there.

The book uses root fields as the setting on which the polynomial's Galois group acts.

4263.title: Root Cause Analysis
4263.heading: Document

4264.sourceSearchName: root cause analysis root cause analysis
4264.title: Root Cause Analysis
4264.heading: Root Cause Analysis
4264.content:
Root cause analysis investigates the conditions that produced a problem instead of stopping at its visible symptom. It reconstructs contributing events, asks why each condition existed, and identifies changes that can prevent or reduce recurrence.

Complex failures rarely have one culpable person or single cause. A useful analysis examines the system, including incentives, information, tools, dependencies, and safeguards.

4265.sourceSearchName: root cause analysis root cause analysis
4265.title: Root Cause Analysis
4265.heading: References

4267.title: Rollback Recovery
4267.heading: Rollback Recovery
4267.content:
Rollback recovery restores an application to an earlier checkpoint after a failure. Computation performed since the checkpoint is lost and must be repeated, so recovery time includes both restart overhead and recomputation.

In a co-scheduled pack, one application's rollback can create load imbalance even when other applications continue normally.

4270.heading: Role-Playing Game
4270.content:
A role-playing game lets the player control one or more characters through adventures or quests, usually with substantial choices about abilities, equipment, and development. Growth in power is common but not logically required.

The genre typically combines exploration, resource management, tactical conflict, character progression, and story. Computer role-playing games implement the world's rules and bookkeeping in software.

4273.title: Role Manager
4273.heading: Role Manager
4273.content:
Role Manager is the ASP.NET Core Identity service that provides APIs for finding, creating, and managing roles. It works with a role store connected to the application's identity database.

The service can be injected into setup or controller code through [[Dependency Injection]]. Database seeding can use it to create required roles only when they do not already exist.

4275.title: ROCK Link Graph

4276.sourceSearchName: rock link graph rock link graph
4276.title: ROCK Link Graph
4276.heading: ROCK Link Graph
4276.content:
A ROCK link graph has one vertex for every record and an edge between two vertices when they have at least one common-neighbor link. The similarity threshold controls the graph's density.

Raising the threshold makes neighbor relations rarer, often increasing the number of connected components. The graph supplies the structure used during agglomerative merging.

4279.title: ROCK Goodness Measure
4279.heading: ROCK Goodness Measure
4279.content:
The ROCK goodness measure scores a possible merge from the number of cross-links between two clusters, normalized for their sizes and the selected similarity threshold. It seeks merges whose link density is stronger than size alone would predict.

ROCK repeatedly selects the pair with the largest positive score. Local and global heaps can maintain those candidates efficiently.

4282.sourceSearchName: robust statistical summary robust statistical summary
4282.title: Robust Statistical Summary
4282.heading: Robust Statistical Summary
4282.content:
A robust statistical summary changes relatively little when a small number of observations are extreme. Medians, interquartile ranges, ranks, and rank correlations can remain representative when means, variances, and ordinary correlations are pulled sharply by an [[Outlier]].

Robustness protects against limited contamination rather than making data quality irrelevant. Extreme observations should still be investigated because they may reveal an error, a distinct population, or a scientifically important event.

4283.sourceSearchName: robust statistical summary robust statistical summary
4283.title: Robust Statistical Summary
4283.heading: References

4285.title: ROCK Clustering
4285.heading: ROCK Clustering
4285.content:
ROCK, Robust Clustering using Links, is an agglomerative method for categorical data. It finds neighbors under a similarity threshold, counts common-neighbor links between records, and merges clusters with the best positive goodness measure.

The process stops at a requested number of clusters or when links disappear. Sampling can make it practical for large databases.

4288.title: Robust Parsing
4288.heading: Robust Parsing
4288.content:
Robust parsing tries to recover useful meaning even when an utterance does not fully match a grammar. It can allow gaps or “holes” for unknown material while preserving recognized phrases and slots.

This tolerance helps with disfluencies and unexpected words, but excessive flexibility causes [[Parser Overgeneration]]. The parser must balance accepting natural variation against inventing unsupported interpretations.

4290.sourceSearchName: robust game verb robust game verb
4290.title: Robust Game Verb
4290.heading: Document

4291.sourceSearchName: robust game verb robust game verb
4291.title: Robust Game Verb
4291.heading: Robust Game Verb
4291.content:
A robust game verb produces an observable response whenever the player reasonably expects an interaction. The response may show success or refusal, but it should still communicate what happened.

Because players use [[Game Verb|verbs]] to investigate other rules, silence can make the system seem unresponsive or inconsistent. Timely [[Feedback]] lets even a failed action teach the relationship between the verb and a [[Game Part|game object]].

4292.sourceSearchName: robust game verb robust game verb
4292.title: Robust Game Verb
4292.heading: References

4294.content:
Robert Noyce proposed an integrated circuit built with the planar silicon process at Fairchild Semiconductor. Deposited conducting paths connected flat components while silicon oxide isolated them.

The design was well suited to photographic patterning and mass production. Patent decisions ultimately divided credit for the integrated circuit between Noyce and Jack Kilby.

4296.heading: Document

4297.sourceSearchName: ripper rule induction ripper rule induction
4297.title: RIPPER Rule Induction
4297.heading: RIPPER Rule Induction
4297.content:
RIPPER rule induction grows rules to cover examples of a selected class and then prunes conditions that do not improve estimated generalization. It repeats this process across classes and performs optimization passes over the rule set.

Pruning guards against highly specific antecedents that explain only accidental training patterns. Class ordering and the default class influence which errors the resulting ordered rule set emphasizes.

4298.sourceSearchName: ripper rule induction ripper rule induction
4298.title: RIPPER Rule Induction
4298.heading: References

4300.title: Risk Chart
4300.heading: Risk Chart
4300.content:
A risk chart orders cases by predicted probability or score and compares accumulated positives, errors, or value across the ranked population. It shows how model performance translates into a limited review or intervention budget.

The chart is most useful when accompanied by a baseline and a clear definition of the risk or benefit accumulated.

4302.title: RMS Voltage
4302.heading: Document
4302.content:
2026-09-17 00:04

Status: #baby

Tags: [[Electromagnetic Induction and AC Circuits]]

4303.title: RMS Voltage
4303.heading: RMS Voltage
4303.content: Root-mean-square voltage is the DC voltage that would produce the same average power in a resistor as a varying supply. For a sinusoid, $V_{rms}=V_0/\sqrt2$ and $I_{rms}=I_0/\sqrt2$. Average AC power for an in-phase resistive load is $V_{rms}I_{rms}$.

4306.title: Risk Variable
4306.heading: Risk Variable
4306.content:
A risk variable records the consequence or value associated with a prediction outcome. It can distinguish errors that have different practical costs even when their classification counts are similar.

Keeping risk separate from the target lets evaluation connect predicted probabilities to decision consequences.

4309.title: Ring
4309.heading: Ring
4309.content:
A ring is a set with addition and multiplication such that addition forms an abelian group, multiplication is associative, and multiplication distributes over addition. The book distinguishes when multiplication is commutative and when a multiplicative identity is present.

Rings generalize integer arithmetic while allowing structures with zero divisors, nonunits, or noncommuting products.

4311.sourceSearchName: ring network topology ring network topology
4311.title: Ring Network Topology
4311.heading: Document
4311.content:
2026-09-22 23:34

Status: #baby

Tags: [[Network Topology and Resource Addressing]]

4312.sourceSearchName: ring network topology ring network topology
4312.title: Ring Network Topology
4312.heading: Ring Network Topology
4312.content:
A ring network topology connects each node to a successor and closes the endpoints into a loop. Communication proceeds around the ring, commonly in one direction, until it reaches the intended node.

The closed path gives the topology a regular forwarding structure, but an unprotected break can interrupt the route. Redundant or bidirectional rings can mitigate that weakness at additional cost.

4313.sourceSearchName: ring network topology ring network topology
4313.title: Ring Network Topology
4313.heading: References

4315.title: Ring Unit
4315.heading: Ring Unit
4315.content:
A ring unit is an element with a [[Multiplicative Inverse]]. If a unit belongs to an [[Ideal]], that ideal must be the whole ring because multiplying the unit by its inverse produces the [[Ring Identity]].

Units are central to [[Ring Localization]], where chosen elements are deliberately made invertible. In a [[Local Ring]], every element outside the unique maximal ideal is a unit.

In the source's elementary ring theory, units form a group under multiplication. This group separates elements that support reversible multiplication from zero divisors and other nonunits.

4318.title: Ring Localization
4318.heading: Ring Localization
4318.content:
Ring localization forms a ring S⁻¹R of fractions r/s whose denominators lie in a [[Multiplicatively Closed Set]] S. Every element of S becomes a [[Ring Unit]], while fractions are identified when a further element of S clears their difference.

The construction is characterized by the [[Localization Universal Property]]. It supports local study, preserves quotient relationships, and corresponds geometrically to restricting functions to an open region of a spectrum.

4320.sourceSearchName: ring level layout ring level layout
4320.title: Ring Level Layout
4320.heading: Document

4321.sourceSearchName: ring level layout ring level layout
4321.title: Ring Level Layout
4321.heading: Ring Level Layout
4321.content:
A ring level layout connects spaces in a loop so the player can continue around and return without reversing direction. Racing tracks are literal examples, but the path can have any visual shape.

Rings support circulation, pursuit, and repeated access to locations. Branches and cross-connections can vary encounters while maintaining an understandable global structure.

4322.sourceSearchName: ring level layout ring level layout
4322.title: Ring Level Layout
4322.heading: References

4324.title: Ring Isomorphism
4324.heading: Ring Isomorphism
4324.content:
A ring isomorphism is a bijective ring homomorphism. It preserves addition, multiplication, zero, the adopted identity, units, and zero-divisor structure.

Isomorphic rings are structurally the same even when their elements are represented differently.

4327.title: Ring Identity
4327.heading: Ring Identity
4327.content:
A ring identity is an element 1 such that multiplying any ring element by 1 leaves it unchanged. In the book's convention, every [[Commutative Ring]] has an identity and every [[Ring Homomorphism]] preserves it.

The identity distinguishes units: a [[Ring Unit]] is an element that can be multiplied by another element to obtain 1. A nonzero [[Field]] requires its identity to be distinct from zero.

The source writes the ring identity as 1_A to keep track of the ambient ring. It also singles out the [[Trivial Ring]], where 0_A = 1_A, before defining characteristics and nontrivial domains.

4330.title: Ring Homomorphism
4330.heading: Ring Homomorphism
4330.content:
A ring homomorphism is a map between rings that preserves addition, multiplication, and the [[Ring Identity]]. Its kernel is an [[Ideal]] of the source ring, and its image is a subring of the target.

The kernel records which elements become zero. The [[First Isomorphism Theorem for Rings]] identifies the image with the source modulo that kernel, connecting homomorphisms directly to [[Quotient Ring]]s.

The book develops ring homomorphisms in parallel with group homomorphisms: kernels are ideals, images are subrings, and the source modulo its kernel is isomorphic to the image. This parallel motivates both quotient rings and the ring version of the fundamental homomorphism theorem.

4333.heading: Rigid Body Fracture and Collision
4333.content: A rigid-body solver moves hard pieces that retain their shapes while colliding under specified forces. To destroy a solid-looking building in the book's example, the model is first fractured into separate parts, then a non-rendering collision object is driven into it. The solver sends the fragments apart, but their visual suitability still depends on the fracture design, materials, timing, and motion blur. A full intact model can be shown until the moment it is swapped for the fractured version. See [[Choreographing Destruction Layers]].

4336.heading: Rigid Object Manipulation
4336.content:
Rigid object manipulation uses the measured pose of a physical object as input to an augmented application. The user translates or rotates a tracked prop, and the system maps that motion to a virtual object, tool, viewpoint, or parameter.

Physical shape and constraints can supply useful affordances and passive haptic feedback. The mapping must account for tracking range, occlusion, clutching, and whether the prop's real geometry is semantically related to its virtual role.

4339.sourceSearchName: right to explanation right to explanation
4339.title: Right to Explanation
4339.heading: Right to Explanation
4339.content:
The right to explanation is a claimed entitlement to meaningful information about an automated decision that affects a person. Its purpose is to make hidden judgment contestable by showing the logic, evidence, and anticipated consequences relevant to the decision.

The scope of the right is disputed. General information about a model does not necessarily explain an individual outcome, while a full technical account may be incomprehensible. A useful right must specify who owes the explanation, what level of detail the affected person needs, and what process allows correction or appeal. It therefore links [[Explainable AI]] with [[Algorithmic Due Process]].

4342.title: Right Coset
4342.heading: Right Coset
4342.content:

They coincide for every group element exactly when H is a normal subgroup.

4345.sourceSearchName: richardson dushman equation richardson dushman equation
4345.title: Richardson-Dushman Equation
4345.heading: Richardson-Dushman Equation
4345.content: The Richardson-Dushman equation estimates the maximum electron current density thermally emitted by a hot surface. Its temperature-squared factor is multiplied by an exponential penalty set by [[Surface Work Function]] relative to thermal energy. Thus a change in emitter temperature or surface material can greatly change available current. Actual [[Thermionic Generator]] current may be lower because electrons in the gap create space charge.

4348.title: Rigel Embedding
4348.heading: Rigel Embedding
4348.content:
Rigel is a landmark-based method for embedding a large graph in the [[Hyperboloid Model]]. It first positions a small set of landmarks so their hyperbolic distances approximate graph paths, then calibrates every other node against those landmarks.

Using far fewer landmarks than nodes reduces multidimensional-scaling cost and permits parallelization. The resulting coordinates approximate node distances, shortest paths, radius, diameter, average path length, and closeness rankings without traversing the full graph for every query.

4351.title: Rhumb Lines and Great Circles
4351.heading: Rhumb Lines and Great Circles
4351.content: A rhumb line crosses every meridian at a constant bearing, making it operationally simple to follow. A great-circle arc follows the intersection of Earth with a plane through its center and gives the shortest surface route between two points. Projection choice determines which of these paths looks straight, as contrasted by [[Mercator Projection for Constant Bearings]] and [[Lambert Conformal Conic Projection]].
